# Landscape: factories x components

How other products handle the components covered in lesson 1: what the plan produces, who drives the plan,
what judges a task done, whether the loop moves on to the next task by itself, and who drives that loop. Each cell is
a paraphrase of a first-party page, with its source URL and the date it was fetched. Cells we could not source are
omitted, not guessed. Task-queue options are not compared per component; they get one Queue column.

**Names are not canonical.** The bold text in each cell is the product's own name for the
capability, taken from its docs. The same stage goes by different names in different factories.

### Factories and coding agents

| Product | Plan output | Plan: who drives | Verify: what judges done | Loop: next task by itself | Loop: who drives | Demoable | Where it takes it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Devin | **Ask Devin**: In Ask Devin the person scopes and breaks down the task in conversation with Devin, which writes a context-rich prompt that starts an Agent session. The page does not say the breakdown carries acceptance criteria or dependencies. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/ask-devin.md), as of 2026-10-13) | **Linear integration**: With Linear, a person starts the work by assigning the ticket, tagging a playbook label or @mentioning Devin (Human), or a Linear automation trigger starts it without manual assignment (Automated). For Ask Devin the page does not label who drives. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/linear.md), as of 2026-10-13) | **unknown**: Devin runs existing tests, lint and type checks in its own environment and iterates until tests pass before submitting a PR. Which checks run is set by the prompt, playbook or repo skill, not by a fixed pipeline. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/essential-guidelines/sdlc-integration.md), as of 2026-10-13) | **Automations**: An automation fires on a trigger (schedule, ticket, GitHub, Slack or webhook) and starts a session with a saved prompt. A finished session choosing the next ticket by itself is not documented. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/automations.md), as of 2026-10-13) | **Automations**: The page says events start sessions automatically, without a person tagging Devin, once a person has created the automation. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/automations.md), as of 2026-10-13) | **free-tier**: The Free self-serve plan lists limited Devin usage, plus access to Devin Review and DeepWiki. ([source](https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve.md), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown |
| Factory (Droid) | **Missions**: Droid builds a structured plan of features grouped into milestones; once the person approves it, the Mission enters Mission Control. Dependency edges between features are not documented. ([source](https://docs.factory.com/missions/overview), as of 2026-10-13) | **Missions**: Mission execution starts once the person approves the plan. ([source](https://docs.factory.com/missions/overview), as of 2026-10-13) | **Validation workers**: Validation workers run at the end of each milestone, verifying its work, and Missions validate their own work by exercising the running application. ([source](https://docs.factory.com/missions/planning), as of 2026-10-13) | **Mission orchestrator**: After each feature or milestone finishes, the orchestrator reviews progress and starts the next work from the plan. ([source](https://docs.factory.com/missions/overview), as of 2026-10-13) | **Mission orchestrator**: After approval an orchestrator manages execution; the person can pause it and talk to it to recover. ([source](https://docs.factory.com/missions/overview), as of 2026-10-13) | unknown | unknown |

([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/use-copilot-agents/research-plan-iterate), as of 2026-10-13) | **Research, plan and iterate**: The person reviews the plan and iterates until it matches their intent before the agent implements it. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/use-copilot-agents/research-plan-iterate), as of 2026-10-13) | **Cloud agent session**: The agent works in its own GitHub Actions environment, where it runs tests and linters to validate changes. How the results decide whether it keeps going before opening the PR is not documented. ### Task-queue options

| Product | Queue | Demoable | Where it takes it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | **Issues, Projects, Cycles**: Issues are Linear's fundamental unit of work; Projects group issues around a shared outcome, and Cycles are a team's repeating planning period. ([source](https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| Jira | **Work items (formerly issues)**: Work items are the building blocks of Jira and can represent a story, bug, task or another work type. ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/what-is-an-issue/), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |
| GitHub Issues | **Issues, sub-issues, Projects**: Issues track bugs, features and ideas; sub-issues add hierarchies between issues, and Projects is integrated with issues to plan and track a team's work. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/learning-about-issues/about-issues), as of 2026-10-10) | unknown | unknown |

## Updating

1. Edit `landscape/matrix.json`. Every populated cell needs `name` (the product's own term,
   or the literal `unknown` if its docs give none), `summary` (a paraphrase of the page),
   `sourceUrl` (https, on a host listed in the product's `allowedHosts`), `asOf`
   (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the day you fetched the page), and `short` (at most 8 words, the text a
   slide cell shows; name the surface when a product has two). Factories carry one cell per
   component; task-queue products carry one `queue` cell.
2. `demoable` and `destination` need the same source and date unless they are explicitly
   `unknown` (`kind: "unknown"` / `summary: "unknown"`).
3. If you cannot find a first-party page that supports a cell, replace it with
   `{ "omitted": "reason" }`; the reason names the pages checked. Never fill a cell from memory.
4. Run `bun scripts/render-landscape.ts` to regenerate this file, then
   `bun scripts/check-landscape.ts` (also run in CI) to validate.
